answer: Seismograph keeper record works as the check: traces kept at one station across years of tremors. The issuer re-attests the record each epoch, and any gap in the history voids the identity. A farm faking 192 aliases needs 192 separate verifiable records of this kind, each checked against the issuing authority, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. A ivory marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the timber ledger turns 192 aliases into 192 bills while the dawn path for the honest stays a single payment.
